Three thousand years of saints, mystics, acharyas, gurus, pirs and reformers who shaped the Indian subcontinent. Arranged by era, by region and by path. Tap any face to read the life.

    On the selection. 96 lives cannot hold a civilisation. This is a representative map, not a complete one, and it deliberately crosses religions: Vedic, Jain, Buddhist, Shaiva, Vaishnava, Shakta, Nath, Sant, Sikh, Sufi and Christian figures sit in one chronology because that is how they actually lived, side by side and often in argument.

    On the dates. Ancient dates are traditional and contested. Where scholars disagree, the commonly cited range is given with "c." for circa. Treat everything before roughly 1200 CE as approximate.

    On the portraits. Images come from Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons and are mostly public-domain paintings, lithographs and early photographs. They are embedded inside this file, so the page works with no internet connection at all. Each one is cropped to the same frame, at the same scale, with the face on the same axis. Three figures, Maitreyi, Bahinabai and Abhinavagupta, have no accepted likeness anywhere and carry an initial rather than a borrowed face. If you republish this page, check each image's licence at Commons first.

    On the sayings. The lines quoted are short, well-known phrases in the original language with plain English renderings written for this page rather than copied translations.
